question: How the original colours the map in the diplomatic (2), intel (6) and theatre (8) modes - every input, constant and the order - when it colours them again, what else each shows, and each one's part of the province tooltip; and how the political mode colours, for comparison.

addresses.name: MapMode_Political_ColourLoop
addresses.comment: **The political map mode's colours** (mode 1). The argument is the CProvinceManager (graphics owner +0x1DC4): its entry vector +0x2C..+0x30 (entry +0 first colour, +4 second, +0xC the CMapProvince) and its CMap at +0x40, whose player (+0x2A88/+0x2A8C) is the viewer. For every entry from 1: b = 1.0 where the viewer's intelligence on the province (+0x370[viewer id], 0 where the id is not under +0x374) is 2 or more, 0.5 below, 0 where the template's simulated byte (+0x13D) is clear. Owner id (+0x330) 0: both colours 0x99999999. Otherwise the owner's colour (CCountry_GetColour, CCountry +0xC30) and, where the controller id (+0x338) differs, the controller's, each through CombineColourBrightness with b and packed: **first colour = the controller's, second = the owner's** - and terrain_2_0.fx draws the second where stripes.dds's alpha is set, 17 pixels of every 64, so the owner is the thin stripe. `ret 4`. Callers: MapMode_Political_Colour (VA 0x6663D3) and VA 0x641D86 (a graphics-owner helper at 0x641D70, called from the console at VA 0x4422E3). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x864000-0x864173: the b selection at 0x86404C-0x864093 (0.5 at 0x15AB304, 1.0 at 0x171DBAC), the 0x99999999 stores at 0x86414B, ebx = owner packed (0x8640D5) and eax = controller packed (0x864125) stored [entry] = eax, [entry+4] = ebx at 0x864133/0x86413E. Stripe share measured off map/terrain/stripes.dds (DXT1, 1-bit alpha decoded: 17 opaque of 64 per row, 26.6%). Wrong if the stores were the other way round, or if GeneralTexture were not the first colour (Map_UpdateProvinceColourTexture's record says Texture1 = first).

addresses.name: MapMode_Political_ColourLoopLobby
addresses.comment: **The political colours with no intelligence and the two colours the other way round** - the front end's and the lobby's map. For every entry from 1: owner id 0 - 0x99999999 both, or black (0, 0, 0, 1) both where the template is not simulated; otherwise first colour = the owner's (CCountry_GetColour packed, no brightness), black where not simulated, and second = the controller's where it differs, else the owner's. `ret 4`. Five callers: VA 0x641DB8 (the graphics-owner helper 0x641D90, called by CGameSetup at VA 0x70B380, 0x70B7E5, 0x70BAD5), CSetHistoryDate::Execute (VA 0x6D6346), CFrontEnd::Enter (VA 0x6EFD90), CGameSetup (VA 0x707FC0, 0x71498A). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x864180-0x864320: owner packed into ebx (0x8641F4), controller into eax where the ids differ (0x864233), the simulated test at 0x86423E replacing ebx by black, [entry] = ebx, [entry+4] = eax (0x864288/0x864293). Callers by findRefs --callers 0x864180 (5). Wrong if the lobby's map were coloured elsewhere - the 'lobby' in the name rests on its callers.

addresses.name: MapMode_Diplomatic_ColourLoop
addresses.comment: **The diplomatic map mode's colours** (mode 2). Viewer P = CMap's player (+0x2A88/+0x2A8C). For every entry from 1, with no intelligence and no simulated test: both colours start grey (0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 1) = 0xFF7F7F7F. **Owner (+0x330) is P**: first = (0, 0.9, 0) 0xFF00E500; second = the same green where P is on the province's core list (+0x344, node +4 the country id, next +0xC), else 0x66666666. **Otherwise**, with S = countries[owner]->diplomacy (+0xE28)[P], the first that holds: S co_belligerent (+0x58) - (0, 0.8, 0.9) 0xFF00CCE5; S dependency (+0x18, a puppet bond either way) - (0, 0.7, 0) 0xFF00B200; the owner's faction (+0xD8) is real (slot 7) and is P's - (0, 0.9, 0.7) 0xFF00E5B2; S alliance (+0x14) - (0, 0.7, 0.7) 0xFF00B2B2; S war (+0x20) - (0.7, 0, 0) 0xFFB20000; else grey; both colours that. **Then, for any province, where P is on its core list the second colour becomes the green.** So cores show as thin green stripes over the relation colour. Guarantees, military access, NAPs and the controller are not asked. `ret 4`. One caller, MapMode_Diplomatic_Colour (VA 0x666A73). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x864330-0x8646AB, each branch's three movss stores into the CColor at esp+0x2C/0x30/0x34 with the constants 0.7 (0x160A2E8), 0.9 (0x160A678), 0.8 (0x174C564), 0.5 (0x15AB304), 1.0 (0x171DBAC); tests at 0x864485 (+0x58), 0x8644C6 (+0x18), 0x864501/0x864533 (faction slot 7, +0xD8), 0x8645AB (+0x14), 0x8645E1 (+0x20); the core walks at 0x86442E and 0x864621; stores [entry] = edi, [entry+4] = ebx at 0x86468B/0x864694. CFaction slot 7 answers mov al,1 (0xA92590), the null faction's xor al,al (0x592360). Packed bytes by truncation of float x 255.0 (CColor::ToPackedArgb). Wrong if a branch's registers were clobbered by the packer call - the decompiler and the reloads after the virtual call at 0x864501 agree they are not.

addresses.name: MapMode_Intel_ColourLoop
addresses.comment: **The intelligence map mode's colours** (mode 6), one colour for both. L = CMap's player's intelligence on the province (+0x370[id]; 0 where the id is not under +0x374). L 0: (0.3, 0, 0) 0xFF4C0000. L 1: (0.2, 0.3, 0) 0xFF334C00. L 2 to 9: g = min(float(L)/9.0 + 0.2, 1.0) (each step in double, rounded to float), and (0.2, g, 0.2) - 0xFF336B33, 0xFF338833, 0xFF33A433, 0xFF33C033, 0xFF33DD33, 0xFF33F933, 0xFF33FF33 for 8 and 9 - **times 0 where the template is not simulated** (black), a test only this arm makes. Alpha 1. Bare `ret`. One caller, MapMode_Intel_Colour (VA 0x6676CB). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x8671F0-0x8673AE: L 0 at 0x867272 (0.3 at 0x15C05EC), L 1 at 0x86729E (0.2 at 0x171618C), the ramp at 0x8672CD-0x867364 (divide by the double 9.0 at 0x160A520, add the double 0.2 at 0x160A260, clamp at 1.0, brightness 1.0/0.5/0 with the simulated test at 0x86730C). Packed values computed by emulating float32 and the packer's truncation. Wrong if the packer rounded rather than truncated (its record and the fldcw RC=11 say truncate).

addresses.name: MapMode_Theatre_ColourLoop
addresses.comment: **The theatre map mode's colours** (mode 8). b = 1.0 at CMap's player's intelligence 2 or more, 0.5 below, 0 unsimulated. First every province both colours grey 0.5b - 0xFF7F7F7F, 0xFF3F3F3F or black. Then for each theatre T of the player's country (CCountry +0x570, list order), k counting from 0: (1) every province of T's +0x60 list gets the colour of **CMap's region number k** (CMap +0x2A40[k], RegionOrContinent_GetColour - the k-th colour of interface/colors.txt in TFH, CMap_AssignRegionAndContinentColours) through CombineColourBrightness with b, or the grey where k is not under the region count; (2) for each area A of T's +0x84 whose group (COwnerArea +0x6C) holds more than one province (AreaGroup_CountProvinces, inlined), CollectTheatreFocusAreas(T, group) and every area F of the answer not controlled by T's country (+0x80; F's controller is its first province's +0x338, 0 for an empty area) and not already done for T: F's provinces get the same colour. Later theatres overwrite earlier. Both colours always alike, so no stripes. `ret 4`. One caller, MapMode_Theatre_Recolour (VA 0x667B10). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x864C40-0x86527E: the grey pass 0x864CE0-0x864D9D (times the double 0.5 at 0x160A308), the theatre walk from [country+0x570] at 0x864DA7, the +0x60 province walk 0x864DE9-0x864F29 with the region test and RegionOrContinent_GetColour/CombineColourBrightness at 0x864ED1-0x864F05 (XMM1 = b), the area walk from +0x84 at 0x864F4C, the sum of +0x2C at 0x864F92-0x864FB1, CollectTheatreFocusAreas at 0x864FE4, the controller test against T +0x80 at 0x865048 and the done-list at 0x865058, k incremented at 0x865229. Wrong if CMap +0x2A40 were not the regions vector (CMap::AssignRegions reads the same).

addresses.name: MapMode_Theatre_Recolour
addresses.comment: **The theatre mode's colouring and refill, only while the mode is 8** (idler +0xD34): the graphics owner's +0x60F8 word = 0 (depot and weather pictures off), HideProvinceObjects98, MapMode_Theatre_ColourLoop, Map_RefreshColourTextures(0), the graphics owner's +0x60DC = 1. Otherwise nothing. `ret 4`. Callers: the theatre setter MapMode_Theatre_Colour (VA 0x667AB8, after it has written mode 8) and CProductionView::RecalculateTheatres (VA 0x7FC931). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and set beside the listing: `cmp [ecx+0xD34], 8` at 0x667AE7, then the four calls; `ret 4` at 0x667B47. findRefs --callers: two. Wrong if the mode test were on another field.

addresses.name: CCountry_GetColour
addresses.comment: *out = the country's colour, the CColor held by value at CCountry +0xC30 (token +0xC34, r g b a +0xC38..+0xC44, opaque +0xC48) - the country file's `color`; returns out, bare `ret`. 16 callers, the two political colourings among them. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: The whole body, 0x4CCCC0-0x4CCCF2: movq [eax+8],[ecx+0xC38]; [eax+4] = [ecx+0xC34]; [eax] = 0x15B6914 (CColor's table); movq [eax+0x10],[ecx+0xC40]; byte [eax+0x18] = [ecx+0xC48]. Wrong if ECX were not a CCountry - the political loops hand it countries_first[owner id].

addresses.name: CProductionView::RecalculateTheatres
addresses.comment: **Rebuilds the player's theatres and repaints the theatre mode**: CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres(the player's country's strategy, CCountry +0x48C, fromScratch = true), then MapMode_Theatre_Recolour(this +0xB0, the idler). Bare `ret`. Its only reference is the production view's constructor, which writes it as the handler of the 0x10-byte member glue at +0xF0 (VA 0x7FB2BB); nothing found subscribes that glue, and CProductionView::AttachButtons hides `theatres_calc_button` instead of attaching anything to it - so *likely* never run in the shipped game. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: The body read 0x7FC860-0x7FC947: `mov edi, ecx`, the player's country from the game state +0xC30/+0xC34, push 1, push country+0x48C, call 0x8A9B10; push [edi+0xB0], call 0x667AE0. findRefs --address 0x7FC860: one reference, the constructor's store. Grep of the constructor and AttachButtons for +0xF0: only the glue's own construction. Wrong if another function subscribes view+0xF0 - not swept for, hence inferred.

addresses.name: ProvinceTooltip_Mode2
addresses.comment: Tooltip builder branch for map mode 2, the diplomatic lines. Only where the owner's id (province +0x330) is not 0 and the template is land (is_land, +0x22): "\n " + the owner's name + ": ", then with S = the player's (game state +0xC30) diplomacy status towards the owner, the first that holds: S war (+0x20) ATWARWITHUS; S co_belligerent (+0x58) OURWARALLY; a vassal bond whose first party, the overlord, is the owner (CDiplomacyStatus_IsVassalWithTargetFirst) OURVASSAL - a key no table of TFH or BlackICE defines; one whose second, the puppet, is the owner (..TargetSecond) DIP_THEY_PUPPET with $OVERLORD$ the owner's overlord's name; S alliance (+0x14) ALLIEDWITHTHEM; S IsGuaranting WEGUARANTEED; S IsGuaranteed THEYGUARANTING; the owner is not the player NEUTRAL; else nothing after the colon. Each rendered with the settings' colours (+0x6C..+0x7B) and appended with no line break of its own. Factions are not asked. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing 0x498A67-0x498F00 and the decompilation: the gates at 0x498A67/0x498A79, the status from [player country +0xE28][owner id] at 0x498AF0, the strings '\n ' (0x15BE5B8) and ': ' (0x15B6B80), the tests at 0x498BB3 (+0x20), 0x498C6F (+0x58), 0x498D29 (0xA48AD0), 0x498DE7 (0xA48A80), then +0x14, IsGuaranting, IsGuaranteed, the player test. Localisation grepped in the install's and BlackICE's csv files (OURVASSAL found only inside the executables). Wrong if a branch appended its own newline - none pushes one.

Land and sea alike. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 3.

Where CCountry::IsFriend(the controller (province +0x334), the player's tag, false) holds: the province's theatre id pair (+0x380/+0x384, read by rva 0x94630), FindPersistentByIdPair, CTheatre_GetUnit - its headquarters - and where both exist "\n(" + the headquarters' name (CUnit slot 7, its +0x16C) + ")". addresses.name: CInGameIdler_RefreshMap
addresses.comment: **The in-game screen's map refresh, every frame**: called once, from CInGameIdler::Update (at VA 0x655EF4), on a join that no branch of Update jumps over (Update has one `ret`, at VA 0x656B80), before CInGameIdler_HandleInput (called at VA 0x656471) and after CInGameIdler_UpdatePanels (called at VA 0x655E2E). `ret 4`. A map mode 17 (theatre) block first, not read through. Then, where the current mode's (+0xD34) entry of the table +0x30 is 1, that mode's **setter** (the mode being already its own, it plays no sound) - 1 MapMode_Political_Colour, 2 MapMode_Diplomatic_Colour, 6 MapMode_Intel_Colour, 5 MapMode_Infrastructure_Colour, 8 MapMode_Theatre_Colour, 17 slot 15 and rva 0x241DC0 then Map_RefreshColourTextures(0), 4 MapMode_Supply_Colour, 7 MapMode_VictoryPoints_Recolour, 9 MapMode_Strength_Colour - and the table's 20 entries zeroed. Then, **where the refresh flags (+0x84) are not 0**: **0x100**, the same setters for modes 1, 2, 6, 5, 8, 4, 7 and 9; **2**, in mode 6 the intel setter; **& 0xF**, the intel setter in mode 6 (once a frame in all), rva 0x266020 (the terrain mode's setter) in mode 0 unless the flags are exactly 2, MapMode_Weather_Set in mode 11, MapGraphics_RefreshByFlags(the CProvinceManager, the flags, &+0x88) and FowTexture_Update; **0x200**, Map_RefreshColourTextures(textures, entries, 0) - both province colour lookups refilled from each province's selected byte as it stands, which is how a selection reaches the map. Then +0x84 = 0, the changed-province list +0x88 emptied (rva 0x4E7DD0), and the graphics owner's +0x60DC = 1. **0x200 is set only by CProvince::OnSelected and CProvince::OnDeselected** (VA 0x49E47D, 0x49E592); Province_SetController ORs **1** (VA 0x4A3585, bit 0) and 0x100 (0x4A35CE); **0x100 also** CMapProvince::SetOwner (0x4A2344), the Apply of the war declaration (0xA146E7), alliance (0xA1A416), military access (0xA247A1), offered military access (0xA26CE7), NAP (0xA2C8CC) and faction (0xA32FA8) actions, CAlliance::Activate (0xA46BC9) and Deactivate (0xA46D79) and SetMilitaryAccess (0xA4A531); ApplyCustomGameSettings, CCountry_Capitulate and the front end's enter 0xF, the in-game enter 0xB; **2** CLocalIntelBoost::Execute (0x9BE658) and CInGameIdler slot 56 (rva 0x272BE0, at VA 0x6731EC: a pass over every province that recomputes its byte +0x36D from where the player's and its allies' units stand and Province_IsHiddenByFog, and sets 2 for each province whose byte changed). Every setter named here also calls Map_RefreshColourTextures, so each of them re-applies the selection lift too. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, sections B.2 and B.9, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: Revised to say the dispatch calls the setters (0x65173B `call 0x666220` etc., the record's names being the setters'), and to complete the 0x100 and 2 writers: a sweep of .text for `or dword ptr [R+0x84], imm8/imm32` found 20 sites - every writer the record already had (the positive control) plus the nine diplomatic ones, each inside the recorded extent of the named function, and slot 56 identified by vtable.py --holding 0x672BE0 (CInGameIdler slot 56 only). A writer by another idiom (load, or, store) would escape the sweep.

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapdraw.md, sections B.7 and B.9, and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 5.
struct_fields.evidence: Comment only: the writers completed by a sweep for `or dword ptr [R+0x84], imm` over .text (20 sites; the record's known writers all among them). Name and type unchanged.

struct_fields.name: color
struct_fields.comment: The country's colour, a **CColor held by value** (its table at +0xC30, token +0xC34, r g b +0xC38..+0xC40, a +0xC44, opaque +0xC48), read from the country file's `color` key by its slot 3 (CColor::Load: each of r g b over 1.0 divided by 255) - which is why the key's loader calls slot 3 on the object here and then copies it to +0xC50. CCountry_GetColour copies it out; the political map colours are made from it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmodescountries.md, section 1.
struct_fields.evidence: Type was CPersistent* (from BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp). CCountry_GetColour (0x4CCCC0) reads +0xC34, +0xC38/+0xC3C, +0xC40/+0xC44 and the byte +0xC48 as the fields of a CColor and writes CColor's table into the copy - an embedded object, not a pointer; the next recorded field is +0xC4C, exactly 0x1C on. Wrong if +0xC30 held a pointer - then +0xC34..+0xC48 would be other fields, and CColor::Load being slot 3 of 'the object here' fits a by-value CColor.

slots_noted: No virtual is named. CInGameIdler slot 56 (0x672BE0) is described in CInGameIdler_RefreshMap's comment only; who calls it was not found, so it is left unnamed.
